text_fidelity_a: Melissa & Doug Farm Sound Puzzle - Wooden Peg Puzzle With Sound Effects (8 pcs) [[VIDEOID:cd72f835dae1d0a3c3f6f6b497d37389]] This is the least child intuitive toy I have ever encountered. Shame on Melissa and Doug- a company that big should have tested this one out before producing. Here's how this puzzle works- as you REMOVE the pieces, the song plays "old mcdonald" but apparently you need to teach your toddler to remove it in the CORRECT order, starting with the farmer and WAITING after removing each piece to hear the song play. Now if you child removes it too quickly they obviously miss all the sounds- if they even hear them within the song. I was expecting to TEACH my toddler animal sounds by hearing them as he placed the pieces. NO such luck. Who in their right mind made a puzzle that plays the sounds when you TAKE out pieces? Most of the kids dump it over so they can make the puzzle. And then there are no sounds when the pieces are placed, disappointingly. Wish I had read reviews, but who would think that Melissa and Doug could RUIN a classic sound puzzle? Somehow, they managed it.

This is a painting of a whole bunch of pictures and other scenes and people from the 1980's. It's based on a painting by Jim Mellet, and his art is amazing! It takes a ton of scenes and people from the 1980's, and turns it into a wonderful painted collage.

The quality of the puzzle is top-notch. The pieces are very thick, and so they fit together well. In my video, you can see that I can actually pick up the entire puzzle, which is usually impossible to do with most puzzles. The backing is a nice blue color, so you can easily tell which pieces are upside down. The border is awesome. The puzzle is surrounded by a red and orange line. This makes the border really easy to put together, and it makes it very easy to identify the edge pieces.

The puzzle is challenging, but it's also very doable. In most puzzles, there's a huge spot of the same color that's very boring, and this puzzle didn't have any of this. I felt entertained and challenged throughout. It's also a great conversation starter, because it has so many iconic people and scenes. I especially liked the Atari, Donkey Kong, Pac-Man, and Mr. T.

Pros:
+Challenging, yet doable
+Fun events and people from the 1980's
+Excellent artwork

Adora My Cuddle & Coo Baby “Cuppy Cake” - Touch Activated Doll with 5 Sounds: She Cries, Coos, Giggles, Kisses Back & Says Momma Just like I had thought before actually receiving this, you are probably thinking that this is a hefty pricetag for a doll that doesn't even have the American Girl logo attached to it... well, move over Pleasant Company (yeah, I said it), because Adora is a new generation of dolls that are not only kid approved (my girls, ages ranging from 6-10, all love their Adora dolls) but it is also parent/caregiver/teacher approved (I would know, as I'm technically all 3, haha). My girls love this doll because she's so cuddly and lifelike, and I love her because I have spent some time actually researching the Adora company... and let me just say THANK YOU for finally coming out with a line of dolls that are crafted from SAFE and nontoxic materials! No more feeling that tiny pang of worry ("mom guilt" lol) whenever my daughter is snuggled up with her doll. I love the peace of mind that comes from knowing the dolls arms, legs, and face are made of vinyl and are BPA free. Finally, a toy company with ethics!

Many of Adoras dolls are machine washable (this particular one has electronics and therefore is not, so care must be taken when wiping the vinyl parts and perhaps spraying a safe vinegar solution on the dolls plush core to keep clean and fresh). Honestly, I can't really comment on the electronic aspect of this doll, as I turned off that feature pretty early (i think it encourages better open-ended imaginative play that way... not to mention less annoying for cranky mommies lol). So you'll have to check other reviews for better details on that function.

All in all, yes, this is not a cheap doll. But in my humble opinion, you are getting a lot of value for your money with this doll. The brand has less expensive plush options too that are just as adorable, less expensive, and even machine washable (we have one and I'll be doing a review soon). The Adora line has a wide selection of dolls and accessories too by the way. I'm actually excited to buy some accessories because I feel like they are very competitively priced and plus it feels good to support such an ethical company that brings so much joy to children.

Grandparents, this is a gift that will not only make you the favorite grandparent, but will also please even the pickiest of health-conscious daughter-in-laws lol.

Two thumbs up for Adora!!

BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer) Mattel has brought a new world to target practice and just plain fun with soft dart guns with this BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster. With no batteries required, the fun is endless. Instead of batteries to power the gun, it is air powered. You have to pump the gun to get enough air pressure to fire the soft darts. Mattel states the gun is for ages 6 and up, but this gun is on the heavy side and requires a bit of strength just to pump it, so I feel ages 7 and up would be a better fit. Even though our 6 year old neighbor didn't want to put this gun down, it was difficult for him to pump it for firing.

The gun is very sturdy being large and made of a heavy plastic. I can see this gun lasting quite a bit of use and not ending up in the trash for a long while. Once pumped it is easy to fire, whether firing one dart or the entire 20 dart clip. At the end of the gun is a special shield you can open up to not only protect yourself from oncoming darts, but your opponents darts will actually stick to this protective shield, allowing you to capture his darts.

Besides the gun there are 30 Smart Stick darts, a 20 dart clip and a Smart Stick target included. The target is great for improving your aim, especially firing one dart at a time. The 20 dart clip is really fun, whether firing at the target or your opponent, as it fires all 20 darts in a matter of a few seconds. It literally fires up to 50 feet, as we shot all 20 darts and several darts went well over 45 feet away. The rapid fire at such a distance is really a lot of fun for the backyard.

Even though these darts are really soft plastic, you will find out that once the children find out how much fun it is to shoot darts at both the target and each other, you may want to purchase the safety eye gear. I don't know if having all 20 darts coming at you from 50 feet away would need some type of eye protection, but I feel it's better to have some type of eye gear on. There is no doubt, this is a safe, sturdy toy with your children wanting to run around and play with this outdoors, gives it 5 Stars. Just getting the kids off the couch away from video games makes it a 5 Star toy, as the exercise alone is worth 5 Stars.
text_fidelity_b: BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Journey Girls 18" Doll, Meredith The Journey Girls dolls are 18" dolls. Clothing-wise, they appear to be compatible with other 18" dolls such as American Girl, Playtime by Eimmie, the Our Generation dolls, or even the 18" Adora dolls. At this price point, they are definitely an affordable play option for younger girls. Like the Adora dolls, they have plastic shoulder and upper torso area and the lower torso is cloth. (The AG, Playtime by Eimmie, and Our Generation dolls all have completely cloth torsos). The Journey Girls dolls do not turn their head well, but their face sculpts are all unique to each doll (again, similar to the Adora dolls, as the Playtime by Eimmie seem to all have the same face sculpt with different skin shades and paint jobs). I personally find the Adora dolls to be my favorite 18" alternative to the American Girl dolls, but they are still at a high enough price point that I would not want to hand one over to my 5 year old for unsupervised play. The Playtime by Eimmie dolls have a full cloth body, making them softer and more huggable than the Journey Girls dolls (and probably more appealing for younger girls), and they are about the same price point. The style of clothing the Journey Girls have, as well as their sculpted plastic upper torsos, they give the impression of teenagers rather than younger girls, which makes them very appealing to the 8-10 year old set.

Meredith is absolutely beautiful and my daughters love her glamorous clothing and hairstyle. An affordable 18" doll option that doesn't make me cringe to give to impulsive young girls for play.
text_fidelity_b: Journey Girls 18" Doll, Meredith

text_fidelity_a:
Folkmanis Grunting Pig Hand Puppet, Standard Packaging, Pink Let’s just say. . . I’m not “squealing with laughter” as it shows on the listing in several places.

First of all. . . This is NOT a pretty pig. It’s kind of “odd” because the color is different in the pictures (the picture of the girl holding it makes it look white with a little tan and black splotches. . . which it is not). The one that I received looks like different shades of tan with some dark splotches. Not the least bit pink. . . not the least bit attractive. I understand that not all pigs are pink in real life. . . and not all pings are “pretty”. . . but when you’re making a toy, then the majority of the time they are pink. . . and they should be at least “not-ugly”, which this one is. . . ugly.

The pictures show the pig standing. This pig does not stand. It lays flat down, with the legs forward. There is nothing stiff in the legs so that it can stand, and it’s obviously made to lay flat.

The “puppet part”. There is a “slit” in the bellow where you put four fingers. You have to find the holes for the fingers for the two front legs. Then you use two fingers to move the mouth up-and-down. Not the easiest thing to do.

The pig “grunts” when you squeeze the “rump” part of the pig. Again, not the best design, in my opinion.

There is a tag that shows that this pig won the 2014 “plush toy” award, which I find very hard to believe.

Finally. . . This is a Made in China toy. . . At the current price it’s WAY too expensive for Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: Folkmanis Grunting Pig Hand Puppet, Standard Packaging, Pink

3Doodler Start Make Your Own HEXBUG Creature 3D Pen Set, Amazon Exclusive, with 2 Additional Insectoid DoodleMold First off, with the START, the main thing to know is it is safe. The temperature of the plastic and the pen tip is low enough, if you accidentally touch it, you won't get hurt. This is great for anyone who isn't fireproof.

It's a new skill. I'm an adult, and I got a bit on my finger the first time I tried it. I am grateful it's not the temperature of normal 3D printing filament (200-300C, and about in range of a soldering iron). With a regular pen, I'd have been in the emergency room. With this, I wiped it off and continued along. That ability, to learn and not worry that much about a beginner mistake, is exactly what attracted me to this. Think of it as training wheels.

The skill is transferable, so once you're confident with this, you can safely move on to the real deal. They make two other models to grow into, and those take pla and abs plastic.

What I didn't like was the lack of clear instructions. There is good stuff on their website, but a better manual would have been appreciated. That's my only ding. Otherwise, this was brilliant. They have additional kits over here [[ASIN:B01CL1FCEY 3Doodler Start Rocket & Robot DoodleBlock Kit]] not just the robot, but a page full of them, if you get tired of hexbugs.

As a die hard Star Wars Fan this Saber has a lot going for it, but a few cons. First the build and look are nice. The sound is also very good. The price is one of the best reasons for getting one. As of today a 40% off coupon making it around $72.00. To me at this price point shows you how much Disney and Star Wars The Black Series is ripping people off.

For the $72.00 you're getting 12 Light Sabers "colors" compare that to $250.00 and higher for one color. Now for the cons the blade is held in place by three set screws and it still has a bit of a lose feeling not much but its there. The other thing is the control button it is a bit cumbersome and by that I mean the holding down or pushing or doing the fast twist while holding button down to change sound fonts. I know some other saber makers use similar features but not this hard to change. One of the sound fonts is not even from Star Wars. I did not know what it was and could not stand it, but you might like. The problem was it took me several tries to change it and it should not be that hard to change.

So even with those two minor faults, this is still a great Saber for the price. As someone who was 10 years old when Star Wars came out, even now holding this and turning it on makes me smile.

"May the Force be with You"
text_fidelity_b: Neo Pixel Light Saber, 20 Light Effects & 17 Sound Fonts Changeable, 41inch Smooth Swing Metal Hilt Light Saber Toys for Boys Girls, Gifts for Boysfriend, Dueling Light Sabers for Cosplay

Paw Patrol Marshall's Transforming Fire Truck with Pop-Out Water Cannons, for Ages 3 and Up I felt like I needed a Paw Patrol car lesson while shopping for cars to fit in the Lookout Tower. Let me tell you there are three main lines I found on Amazon, Spin Masters website, and in Target/Walmart:
- Basic Vehicles
- Transforming Vehicles
- Ultimate Rescue Vehicles

I wanted cars that would fit the Lookout Tower, and finally figured out that although some people may say that the Ultimate Rescue line fits in the tower, they are the biggest of the three lines and some reviews say those are too big.
The Basic Vehicles are the original vehicles (the Basic Chase car comes with the Lookout Tower) and those were originally intended to be the cars for the tower. The Basic Marshall car is simply called “Marshall’s Fire Fightin Truck”. However, the Basic line is hardest to find, and they are currently either marked up by third party sellers on Amazon or I could only find one or two Basic cars at each Target I visited.

Enter this Transforming line. They are a bit smaller than the Ultimate Rescue, and I was able to find them for $12.99 each on Amazon. They all have a little button that pops out the pups gear. My kids like popping out Marshall’s water cannons and they can reset them themselves (ages 2.5 and 4).

Long story short, this will work in the Lookout Tower. Best of luck finding them all for your kid.
text_fidelity_b: Paw Patrol Marshall's Transforming Fire Truck with Pop-Out Water Cannons, for Ages 3 and Up

text_fidelity_a: Chompin' Charlie Game - Feed The Squirrel Acorns And Race To Collect Them When They Scatter - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath This is a perfect addition to the Fall basket. There are always lots of books about squirrels and acorns to add to the fall line-up and this game goes with them well. It's a great companion to those books and we've all had fun with it. There's also a little puzzle to go with the game, which adds more fun to the squirrel/acorn focus. To play the game, the players take turns rolling a die. The color/number that is rolled is what color and how many(up to 2) acorns you put into Charlie's mouth. Once he gets full, the acorns roll out the holes that are in the tree trunk that Charlie stands on. Using only one hand, the players race to collect the acorns. The first player to fill up their acorn stash card wins. The rules say that if a player rolls a certain color and it's not in the main stash of acorns, that player has to take one of their collected acorns or take one from another player. Taking from another player won't be for all families, but it can be adapted, if desired. Also, with the acorns rolling everywhere, it's tricky finding the best place to play. The acorns will roll off the table, but if on the floor, they could roll under things, like couches, if it's a smaller space. Our home is small, so we try to put up little "walls" to make sure the acorns don't roll under things. Overall, it's a fun game and the quality of it is nice, too. It's a simple game that's a great way to add a bit of joy to a day.
text_fidelity_b: Chompin' Charlie Game - Feed The Squirrel Acorns And Race To Collect Them When They Scatter - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath

OH! MY GIF Moving Collectibles Toy with 6 Exclusive Dancing GIFbits, Multicolor (24116) GIFs are popular among older kids and among adults- possibly even more so with adults. For the GIF lover in your life, I present to you OH! MY GIF Moving Collectibles Toy with 6 Exclusive Dancing GIFbits.

This set includes six different GIF and to make things more fun, each one features movements of some sort. You activate the movements by pushing or moving different sections of the item. It works a little different from one to the next. With the dog, there is a wind- up on its back and it will therefore continue to move on its own. With the others, you have to activate manually.

Each of the six GIF in this set feature cool, vivid colors and they are cute to look at. The issues I can see are with specific pieces. The donut, for example, doesn’t have a base and is therefore a little more of a problem to stand up, since it falls down easily. And the different GIF are inconsistent in what you have to do to make them move. No biggie, just something to keep in mind. For added fun, there is an app you can download, scan included cards, and have the different GIF on your phone.

This is a fun enough set of GIF and if I could change one thing, it would be to have a wind- up on all six of them, and not just the dog, because then you could wind them all up and let them dance the night away. Other than this, the GF Moving Collectibles is a still a fun set for kids and adults alike.

Elmer's Color Changing Liquid Glue | Makes Slime That Changes Color As You Play, Dark to Light Green, 5 oz. This glue is fun! But not when it’s used as a glue.
When it’s used as a glue it just stays purple.
When this glue is used as a slime is where it really shines.
I cut the bottle in half with some kitchen shears and then scraped the glue out - this glue is thicker than most glue I’m used to.
This glue mixes easily with slime activators to create slime.
When the glue gets warm it turns pink.
If you want a slime that is a light purple/pink then just simply mix this glue with some regular white glue until the desired color is achieved.
My daughter got some of this glue slime on her white dress. I washed her dress in hot water and after the wash there was still some coloring on the dress. I then pretreated it and washed it, the dress came out clean!
This glue as a slime is fun to use I even enjoyed watching it change from purple to pink!

text_fidelity_a:
Mega Bloks Call of Duty Desert Tank Building Set Ok first let me say, we are a "it's Lego or its crap" family. My kids evangelize on the evils of Megablocks and other brands they consider knock offs. But this is such a well engineered and detailed set that my fifteen year old wasn't even grudging when he said, this is a really good set.

And he's right, the detail on this set is super impressive. My son loves it for what seems like very authentic design from a war historian rather than a gamer, so maybe a fan of COD would like it even more.

This is a very challenging build, filled with small parts and unlike Lego that pre bags parts so you can open a single bag to do the first couple pages of instructions, mega blocks has you open 80% of the bags for the first few pages. You end up with an impressive pile of pieces out there. Also unlike Lego, mega blocks will create molded pieces specific to a model so realism can be pushed farther than Lego does. In this set, the body is filled with parts that are not just molded to shape but also in color to seem camouflaged or dirty from use. This truly lends a wonderful realism to the model. We also appreciated that markings are screen printed onto pieces rather than using stickers. Kudos for doing that it makes it feel like a quality set.

I do notice a bit more brittleness in the blocks and brick for brick the quality does not seem to match lego, but I can do little but rave over this set. It is beautiful, it took my son and I working together to get this done in several hours. And once done, this is a beautiful set for display.

Well done Mega Block, you are doing what I thought was impossible, you are winning us over from Lego.

*** additional

My son wanted me to mention that the instructions were hard, I would use challenging. But one thing I did forget, I am partially colorblind and often found it hard to distinguish colors in the instructions if it was not daylight.
text_fidelity_b: Mega Bloks Call of Duty Desert Tank Building Set

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Glow Book I never really thought I would be calling any toy a godsend, but the Crayola Glow Book has done something for my ten-year-old son that none of his school teachers (and certainly not his art teacher) has been able to do. I've tried, too. I've tried asking, showing, cajoling, ordering, limiting privileges, exaggerated sighing, and using his full name, but my child's penmanship is abysmal and his art skills mostly stink.

The reason for this is relatively straightforward: in my family, kids develop their fine motor skills later than most kids do. My parents and teachers made me work at it, but I at least was getting a lot of practice all the time. My child goes to a school where he gets to type a lot of his assignments. He's learned a lot in art about color and perspective and design, but he gets extremely frustrated trying to execute what's in his head, so he stopped enjoying drawing and painting pretty much as soon as he hit kindergarten.

When I ordered this, I thought it was going to turn out to be just a gimmicky gadgety thing he'd use once and then I'd get to use it to leave notes my husband would have to work to ignore, but my son loves it. He can write, draw, erase, illuminate, and animate without having to commit anything to paper or to critical eyes (except his own). Because the illustration plates are layered, if he's happy with one part but not another, he can re-do the one without having to worry about smudging or wrecking the other. As a result, he is spending time using his fine motor skills, they are improving, and he is much happier with the work he is doing.

I gave this five stars for fun, based on his recommendation. I rate it five stars for educational value and five stars overall for how much help it has been in an area in which my child needed some help. I gave it four stars for durability. It feels a little flimsy, but it's holding up well so far.

UPDATE: When you exhaust the markers that come with this, you can use dry erase markers on it. They're actually a little bit easier to see and work with, they come in tons of colors, and they clean right up.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Glow Book

text_fidelity_a:
Journey Girls 18" Doll, Callie The Journey Girls dolls are 18" dolls. Clothing-wise, they appear to be compatible with other 18" dolls such as American Girl, Playtime by Eimmie, the Our Generation dolls, or even the 18" Adora dolls. At this price point, they are definitely an affordable play option for younger girls. Like the Adora dolls, they have plastic shoulder and upper torso area and the lower torso is cloth. (The AG, Playtime by Eimmie, and Our Generation dolls all have completely cloth torsos). The Journey Girls dolls do not turn their head well, but their face sculpts are all unique to each doll (again, similar to the Adora dolls, as the Playtime by Eimmie seem to all have the same face sculpt with different skin shades and paint jobs). I personally find the Adora dolls to be my favorite 18" alternative to the American Girl dolls, but they are still at a high enough price point that I would not want to hand one over to my 5 year old for unsupervised play. The Playtime by Eimmie dolls have a full cloth body, making them softer and more huggable than the Journey Girls dolls (and probably more appealing for younger girls), and they are about the same price point. The style of clothing the Journey Girls have, as well as their sculpted plastic upper torsos, they give the impression of teenagers rather than younger girls, which makes them very appealing to the 8-10 year old set.

The packaging indicated Callie is from Japan, and she definitely has more almond-shaped eyes than Meredith. Her light skin, brown hair (instead of black), and eye shape reminded my bi-racial girls of themselves. That is the true gift of doll lines that have unique face sculpts, to provide a mirror so all little girls can have a doll that resembles them, as well as a truly diverse line of dolls.
text_fidelity_b: Journey Girls 18" Doll, Callie

text_fidelity_a:
Munchkin We've only had the game for a few days, but so far we've played it a total of six times, you figure each game is one hour long, so basically we've gotten six hours of fun for the affordable price of under twenty bucks. So, way less than we'd spend if my family went out to see a movie and best of all, we didn't even have to leave the house.

A little bit about the game, it seemed a bit complicated at first.

We followed the directions, give each player four cards each from the two stacks, that part was basic, but we ended up folding and unfolding the game play instructions trying to figure out what to do next.

Basically, each player tries to level up. Levelling up can be achieved in just a few ways, 1. defeating a monster (which you can only do if you have enough levels, which means you may need to, 2. buy a level, by selling magical items or 3. get a level up treasure card.

The game seemed a bit slow at first because each player starts with just one level which is too low to start fighting monsters. But the game picked up when we'd all gotten to level three. The monsters can be defeated by more than one player, so one minute I was sabotaging my son's chances at winning another level, the next we were fighting flying frogs together and sharing in the loot!

The cards themselves give you directions, telling you to add 5 to fight a monster (very useful card to use against your opponents) or that certain magical items can only be used by certain characters; dwarves, elves, etc.

By the time we played a third time, we knew the game well enough to start levelling curses at each other and how to steal each others treasures.

Munchkin has a lot of extender packs, munchkin zombie, munchkin the guild (I just bought this one, yay!) etc. that add to the original game set.

Since we play a lot of games here at home, monopoly, settlers of catan, telepathy, zombie dice, risk, etc. figuring out the basic rules wasn't terribly difficult, but I think looking at a few munchkin blogs could prove helpful (yep, there really are munchkin blogs.)
text_fidelity_b: Munchkin

text_fidelity_a:
Kubros Despicable Me Minion Building Kit I am a Lego fan, but I kept that in mind as I reviewed this, not wanting it to make my review unfair.
So, lets start with the kit. The pieces do not fit together as well as Lego pieces do. That’s not a huge thing, but it’s a little annoying with some of the steps.
I have to say that the instructions are much better than Lego ones –MegaBlox devised a very clear way to show what piece to put, and where to put it. That was nice. However, they lace the style Lego shows – if this were a Lego set, it would be hollow – allowing things to go inside it – this set is solid, no room inside for anything. The feet fall off easily, which gets old fast.

Plus there are many “special” bricks that will limit the owners ability to make other things out of the set. Although, that is moot if you have a sizable MegaBlox collection already.

The finished piece is nice – a little boxy – think Minions meets Minecraft.

My issue is the price though. If you look at Lego sets (aside from brand ones like Disney and some of the collectable ones) the cost is around 10c per brick.
This set works out at almost 30cents per brick. Three times the cost of a comparably sized Lego set.
The quality does not warrant that price. Despite the added value of the Despicable Me brand. If it was rounder, more interactive, or had stronger feet I would be inclines to give it a better score

If the shortcomings don’t bother you, and your life *needs* all things “Despicable Me” then you will enjoy this.
If someone else is paying for it, you will find it a bargain.

Otherwise I would recommend you get your Despicable Me and building set fix from a better product.
text_fidelity_b: Kubros Despicable Me Minion Building Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Alex DIY Happy Little Loom Kit Kids Art and Craft Activity It's not wide enough to make a scarf, not for most kids. There is very little yarn included. You will need worsted weight for this kit.

The last point leads into my main issue with this. It does not provide enough information. You know you need yarn, but yarn varies in weight from lace (even gossamer) to super bulky. These terms refer to how thick the yarn is. Buy too thin, and the project will look terrible. Buy too thick and the yarn won't fit into the weft holes. You need worsted weight, and the only reason I know this is I knit and I recognized the yarn. The kit doesn't tell you.

If you hit a knot in the yarn, as I did, you should not keep going. Cut at the end of the row (the instructions don't tell you this) then start on the right side again (the instructions don't tell you this) and whenever you stop or start, leave a tail long enough to weave in later (nothing about weaving in tails is covered -- you're just supposed to know how to do that).

If you want to do the purse, for example, cut 15 strands at 32 inches each (not explained) so that they turn into 16 inch strands when doubled. You can get away with cutting 16 inch and having them single stranded, but it isn't optimal, especially when you are tying pairs at the end. And maybe do it with a yarn not in this kit. They barely provide enough yarn in this kit, and no one wants their kid playing yarn chicken and getting upset. It's cheap yarn. Get a good amount.

When you start the yarn, it is shipped in a center pull ball. While the value of balls is explained a little (I suppose over leaving it in a loose skein or hank to tangle on itself) the concept of center pull isn't touched on. Dig into the ball and get the end inside. That way the ball stays still while you work.

You don't really need the tool to guide the yarn back and forth, but it should have come with a comb to push it down and keep it even, a trick especially hard when you move the piece along down the thread. That's perhaps the biggest design flaw in this. It tends to make the work uneven because it's slid and it leaves gaps where the next section starts. That can mostly be worked out by blocking the piece after (another technique not covered -- wet it, stretch it into the shape you want and even out the rows, and pin it down to dry.)

This is a great kit for someone who already knows a lot about yarn projects like crochet or knitting, or of course weaving. For a first yarn craft, a kid is going to need some help, ideally from someone who knows a lot about yarn projects.
text_fidelity_b: Alex DIY Happy Little Loom Kit Kids Art and Craft Activity

text_fidelity_a:
7 Wonders We're a game playing family. With 84 board/card games and counting, I feel like something of an expert on board games. This was an exceptionally good game. Unlike some strategy games, there doesn't seem to be any one strategy that's going to always work. You have to be flexible, depending upon which wonder you end up with, the cards you get, and the strategies your opponents are using. You have to pay particular attention to the strategies of your nearest neighbors on either side because many actions and many cards play off of them. No cards or actions play directly off of an opponent who is not your neighbor. That, too, is a nice feature. It's not that you shouldn't watch what the people across the table are doing, but it's more important to know what the guys to the right and left are doing. Especially when you're dealing with higher numbers of players, that makes it easier to keep up with. That's a big part of why it works as well for 7 players as it does for 3. That, and the fact that game play is simultaneous -- no turn taking! So there's very little down time and the games moves quickly.

The only reason I didn't give this game 5 stars is that the game comes with rules for a 2-player variation that I do not believe is very good. I was hoping that this would be a game I could play with my husband after our (young) kids went to bed, but after trying several times we both agreed on two things:

1) There are much better 2-player games.
2) This game is much better with 3-7 players.

For those reasons, we will only pull it out when we have friends over. But it really, really is a top-notch game for the right number of players. I mostly wrote this review to caution people who are considering buying it more for it's two-player extendability than anything else.
text_fidelity_b: 7 Wonders

Really, as mentioned at the start, there isn’t much to say about Schleich beyond the fact that quality quality quality is the mantra. LEGO City Race Boat Transporter 60254 Race Boat Toy, Fun Building Set for Kids (238 Pieces) This LEGO CITY RACE BOAT TRANSPORTER BUILDING SET ((60254) New 2020, 238 Pieces) is fairly easy to build--the difficulty is what I’d call “normal” for a City-themed set. City sets are among my favorites, because they include fire trucks, police stations, buses, trains, beachgoer minifigs, space stations, and all the rest of the things that a bustling city (or the airspace above it) needs. This particular set is aimed at ages 5 and up.

The set contains all the pieces required to build three separate items: a semi-trailer truck (for towing the race boat), a trailer for hauling the race boat, and a race boat. (You can use the truck’s trailer hitch to tow other things that you build, of course.)

The “Xtreme” graphics are NOT printed on the pieces, but are applied with stickers. (I hate stickers, too.) Applying stickers is made easier if you first stick a corner to something long and thin (e.g., a spudger or a plastic knife) so that you can better control the placement on the element. A good thing about LEGO stickers is that they can be removed and replaced (like Post-Its) if you get them misaligned.

The LEGO elements are compatible with other City sets and with all regular LEGO sets (but not with DUPLO sets, which have extra-large pieces for very young builders). The Race Boat Transporter set is another fine addition to the extensive collection of City sets.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO City Race Boat Transporter 60254 Race Boat Toy, Fun Building Set for Kids (238 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Dungeons, Dice & Danger – an Easy to Learn Roll and Write Strategy Game for Ages 12 and Up I have been enjoying this as a solo game but am happy that it won't be hard to teach friends.

Unlike some games there isn't a finite number of turns...the game ends when someone defeats the boss then each players points are tallied. I like that aspect a lot.

There are some "power" type blocks that benefit all players when one player has success with it.

The art is very cool and whimsical. The paper is sufficient but not very heavy duty. You get plenty of maps...there are 4 of each distinct map design. It's a busy map and I plan on taking the cheapest route possible and using regular sheet protectors and dry erase markers.

I'm not liking the wooden dice at all. For the money I would have really liked some fancier dice. Maybe bigger...maybe more colorful.
You get 4 short presharpened pencils that ...don't have erasers and your first game or two you might need to correct something.

Basically this could have been a print and play. There's nothing at all spectacular about the contents.

My personal little gripe is I don't see how you can be in two places at once. You can attack the map from different sides of the map moving in from starter sections.

That's seems like a lot of negativity but it is a fun little game anyway. You can play it on a small table or most places since there aren't components other than a map and the dice. Also this can encourage people to play who maybe aren't that into games since you don't unload tons of intimidating cards, counters and pieces.

It's a very fine experience. It could've been better for the money though.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Dungeons, Dice & Danger – an Easy to Learn Roll and Write Strategy Game for Ages 12 and Up

Hot Wheels 20-Pack of 1:64 Scale Toy Sports & Race Cars, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary) It might seem as if 20 cars is too much at once. Nope! It is wonderful.

Days as a five year-old were best filled with playing in complete abandon. The freedom proffered by youth needed only a few toys to complete the ever-present joy. A few toys which mattered included several tattered but friendly books, a truck or two, an odd shovel and bucket, and, the coup de grace, a Hot Wheels car. Mattel makes a track as well, but a well-made car could take a boy places. This set of 20 is what kindergartners drool over.

A boy has everything in this set: vehicles of all colors, a few truck varieties, some funny looking cars. There are plenty, and frankly, since a few will invariably wind up lost under the couch, eaten by the dog, and buried with other treasures in the garden, having 20 quickly becomes justified.

Why a Hot Wheels car? Because they are made with hard steel. They are painted with a slick color. They hold up to frequent tastings, sand grindings, dirt smearings and other nonsense that comes with power racing in a sandbox. Sticky chocolate wipes off with warm water, and grime comes out with a good spray under the faucet.

The wheels themselves have a bounce peculiar to a genuine Hot Wheels vehicle. That's how my brother and I made sure it had adequate fuel. Ten bounces should be enough, we figured, and usually, we were right.

I fully recommend the "Hot Wheels 20-Car Gift Pack."

Anthony Trendl
AmericanSpeechwriter.com
